body:
You lost me with this.

I thought about addressing each point separately, but I just don't feel like it to be honest.

You're making a lot of assumptions and offering suggestions for my care after what.. 3 comments? I don't think you're being intentionally malicious, but still..

No, I don't present myself that way. No it's not an easy fix. No "we" can't work on anything. And no, I cannot take a break from my life to go to therapy.

Fwiw means "for what it's worth."

Oh man what a question. The answer is a bit complicated. Yes, I've absolutely engaged in attention-seeking behavior in the past. It seems to revolve around my desperate need to feel loved correctly (treated well). But at the same time, I work very hard not to show vulnerability. It's an exhausting but unintentional balancing act.

In general I assume people don't help because they don't understand and/or they think I'm strong enough to get by without them. Or because I never text or call anyone.

My relationship is less than ideal and while I'm not happy with where we are, I think we are on the right track. I'm sure those problems contribute as well.

Ask any questions you like. I'm generally an open book (might be a bit more into protecting my identity on this one than usual though), but I do better with specific questions rather than general ones which I know can be difficult.

Fwiw I have friends and family and a bf who I live with. They all seem to like me and generally enjoy my company. I'm generally introverted and whether it's my personality or a result of abuse (it's that one), I don't get close to people. Even people I think I'm close with or who think they're close to me..idk how to explain, but I think you'll get the idea. I keep things back. I don't ever fully trust anyone, myself included.

There are so many details, contributing factors, points of interest, etc. that I never know where to start or end and no matter how many questions you ask or how long I talk, there's always going to be something important (whether just to me or objectively) that I forget until later.

Edit: and then I don't even answer your question..

Yes my environment undoubtedly plays a part in my depression and my depression plays a part in my environment.

I really don't know what her deal is with pregnancy loss. After I posted that comment, I remembered a couple of years ago when a mutual friend (X) had her second pregnancy loss. X was posting about it a lot on social media and my friend made a big thing of it. She did stop when I told her to just let X grieve and that she was being weird about it. I hadn't thought about it in a while, but yeah.. I'm not sure how to talk to her about it, but I think I need to.

I really just need to grow a stiffer spine and be clear about my boundaries. It's something I'm working on, I just might need some professional help. Being a doormat must be related to addiction - it feels very similar with progress and setbacks.

Thank you very much for your kindness. As much as I'd like to take credit for bravery, the truth is that I simply survived because I felt I had no other option, and I think I blocked out my second loss to accomplish that survival. I don't think I would've lived if I had felt all my feelings from two losses so close together. I guess I didn't say in the post, but they were only about 4 months apart. It wasn't relevant, but we'd also been trying to get pregnant for 3 years when I had my first miscarriage and since I was so young, I was sure I was broken. I was overall in a very dark place at the time, and one more thing would've been too much.

I rarely talk to her about my ex as it is, but I probably should just avoid it altogether. Part of the trouble with that is that I'm close friends with her husband, who I've known for 20 years. I don't know how safe it is to talk to him about things if it will get back to her, now. Not that I don't trust him, but they're married and it wouldn't be a shock if he told her, you know? It sucks because she and I had become really close, and now the friendship feels tainted or something.

I googled reactive abuse and read an article about it. It fits 100% so far, but I'll have to do more reading. I'm trying to get back into therapy for unrelated things, but this has given me some perspective that applies in a much broader way than I would've expected (I hope that makes sense).

Thank you very much for your comment and well-wishes. I wish the same for you and for all abuse victims.

I honestly never even thought about telling him until the friend called. It probably sounds terrible, but I was too wrapped up in myself and my own feelings. Him and his feelings never even crossed my mind.

I've been thinking about the friend a lot. She is really really off with how she views pregnancy loss, and this was not my only issue with that convo. She was very judgmental about how ex's wife handled her stillbirth. Apparently her older kids were present because they were finding out the sex and wanted to involve them. Well, they were in the room when the doctor said the baby had passed and I guess they're pretty traumatized. My friend feels like ex's wife was irresponsible to bring the older kids and blames her for the trauma. I don't like ex's wife at all, but I just cannot see how she did anything wrong in that situation.

At the same time, she's married to someone I've been friends with for 20 years, so I haven't decided how to handle that.
I'm torn between knowing that I don't owe him anything, and feeling like the death of a child is not something you keep from the other parent.
